units.t: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions and Decimals
Number and the Laws of Arithmetic

unit.title: The Number System
unit.blurb: Place value in whole numbers and decimals with up to two decimal places, multiplying and dividing by 10 and 100, and rounding decimals.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand the value of each digit in whole numbers and decimals with one or two decimal places, and multiply and divide by 10 and 100.

O2.t: Round numbers with one decimal place to the nearest whole number.

p: The digits after the decimal point are **tenths** and **hundredths**. In 347.25 the 2 is worth 2 tenths (0.2) and the 5 is worth 5 hundredths (0.05).
× 10 moves every digit **one place left**; ÷ 10 moves every digit one place right. × 100 and ÷ 100 move **two places**.

lesson.t: Why tenths and hundredths continue the pattern
p: Each place is 10 times the place to its right. Going right past the ones, the places are tenths (÷10) and hundredths (÷100).

lesson.q: What is the value of each digit in 3.47?

lesson.t: Find the value of a decimal digit
p: First place after it: tenths; second: hundredths.

lesson.t: Do not just add a zero

p: To round a number with one decimal place to the nearest whole number, look at the **tenths** digit.
If it is **5 or more**, round up. If it is less than 5, round down. 7.6 → 8 and 7.4 → 7. 7.5 rounds up to 8.

lesson.t: Why we look at the next decimal place
p: Rounding to the nearest whole number asks: is it nearer this whole or the next? The tenths digit tells us.

lesson.q: Round 7.46 to the nearest whole number and to 1 decimal place.

p: Find the two numbers it is between.
To round 4.49 to the nearest whole number, look at the tenths digit, 4: it rounds down to 4.
